title: Worktree-creation soft-fail can run a job against another job's tree
description:
_checkout_bundle_branch_for_job (runner.py:2720) is soft-fail by design: if create_job_worktree fails the job PROCEEDS. That rationale predates B1 and its docstring still describes the pre-B1 world — 'falls back to pre-Step-30 behavior (commits land on whatever branch is current)'. That was safe when the fallback was one shared checkout sitting on some branch.

After B1 the fallback is different in kind. create_job_worktree returns BEFORE _point_ports_link when 'worktree add' fails (worker.py:1588-1594), so /work/DeltaPorts keeps whatever it pointed at. Normally that is ports-main, because destroy_job_worktree repoints on job end. But if a previous job crashed or its teardown failed, the link still points at THAT job's worktree — so this job's agent edits a dead job's tree and its commits land on the dead job's branch. Cross-job contamination, which is the exact thing B1 exists to prevent.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL: create_job_worktree returned ok=False twice during B1 bring-up, both on the first call after deploying new code, never reproduced across 12 fresh cycles and never explained. The soft-fail path has fired for real.

CANDIDATE FIXES, not chosen: (a) hard-fail the job when the worktree cannot be created — the trade-off the original rationale rejected, but the cost of proceeding is now much higher than 'lost isolation'; (b) force the link to the idle target (ports-main) before proceeding, so a soft-fail degrades to the main checkout rather than to an arbitrary dead job's tree; (c) assert the link resolves to this job's worktree before any worker.* call.

(b) is the smallest change that removes the contamination while keeping the original soft-fail intent.

Also update the stale docstring rationale in runner.py:2731-2739 whichever way this lands.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A failed worktree creation cannot leave a job editing another job's tree. 2. The soft-fail rationale in _checkout_bundle_branch_for_job describes post-B1 behaviour. 3. The verify/confirm path (_checkout_verify_branch_for_job) gets the same treatment or a documented reason it differs.

title: Two in-chroot call sites still located the tool in the ports tree (runner could not start)
description:
Missed by the X5/X6 repository split. Both invoked the wrapper as "$DELTAPORTS_ROOT/dportsv3", which is two mistakes at once: DELTAPORTS_ROOT is the ports tree, not the tool checkout, and in this repo the repo-root 'dportsv3' name belongs to the Python package rather than the wrapper (the wrapper is bin/dportsv3). layout.py:50 documents that exact trap; these two consumers were not repointed.

  * health.py:236 _check_dports_compose — SEVERITY: total. sh returns 127, the check reports broken, _aggregate turns any broken check into a broken env, and _gate_blocked pauses the whole runner loop. The runner could not process a single job in any env built after the split.
  * worker.py:1746 validate_dops — the convert agent's cheap dsl check always failed.

Confirmed /work/DeltaPorts/dportsv3 does not exist post-split by inspecting a real DeltaPorts checkout: the repo has no dportsv3 at its root, so there was no stale vendored copy masking this.

CORROBORATING SIGNAL, worth remembering as a smell: build_env_dict has exported POLYTROPOS_ROOT since the split (helpers.py:148) and NOTHING consumed it except the showenv helper and tests. A new env var with no readers meant the consumers were never repointed.

WHY THE X5 VERIFICATION MISSED IT: criterion 5 was verified on x6 by provisioning an env, not by running the runner loop. Provisioning uses TOOL_BIN and is correct; the health gate and the agent tool path are only exercised once the runner actually starts, which poly-4kr blocks.

FIXED: both call sites now use "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/dportsv3". tests/test_chroot_tool_path.py greps the whole agent package for the old shape and asserts the built command text for both helpers; mutation-tested by reverting each fix.

STILL OPEN, low priority: docs/agentic-architecture-backlog.md:1214 shows the old invocation. Historical design record, but a copy-paste re-infection source.

NOT VERIFIED IN A REAL CHROOT — no way to run the services yet (poly-4kr). The fix is a path correction with a unit guard; an end-to-end confirmation still owes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. No agent-package call site locates the wrapper under the ports tree. 2. A post-split env passes the compose health check so the runner does not pause. 3. Verified in a real chroot once poly-4kr unblocks.

title: reconcile/diff_tree silently miss content changes: _DeepDircmp.phase3 override never runs
description: fsutils._DeepDircmp overrides phase3 to force cmpfiles(shallow=False) so classification is content-based. The override is NEVER CALLED. filecmp.dircmp.methodmap is built in the class body and captures the BASE class function objects; dircmp.__getattr__ dispatches via self.methodmap[attr](self), which invokes dircmp.phase3, not the subclass override. Verified on Python 3.11.12 (DragonFly x6) and 3.11.14 (macOS): methodmap['same_files'] is <function dircmp.phase3>, and two files with equal size+mtime but different content classify as same_files. Consequence: reconcile() skips the copy and diff_tree() reports no difference, so a real content change is silently lost. Masked on macOS/APFS because nanosecond mtime makes consecutive writes differ (1787237401268667053 vs ...740553), so the accidental shallow compare still sees a diff. Exposed on DragonFly/HAMMER2 where consecutive writes share an mtime (both 1787237404520528000) - the production platform. Realistic trigger: a same-length edit such as DISTVERSION=1.2.3 -> 1.2.4 written in one tick would not propagate to the live composed tree. Surfaced as 3 suite failures on x6: test_fsutils_reconcile.py::test_content_change_updates_dst, ::test_symlinks_with_different_content_replaced, test_fsutils_diff_tree.py::test_content_difference_is_reported.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Content-based classification actually runs - do not rely on overriding phase3. 2) A regression test pins the failure mode directly: equal size AND equal mtime, different content, must classify as a difference on every platform (force mtimes equal with os.utime so it fails on macOS too, rather than depending on filesystem granularity). 3) The three x6 failures pass. 4) Audit other dircmp/filecmp subclassing for the same methodmap trap.
notes: Hash correction: the fix commit is 4af664d (referenced as 06546ff before the attribution trailer was stripped and the unpushed commits rewritten).
close_reason: Fixed in 06546ff. _DeepDircmp.phase3 was never invoked (dircmp.methodmap binds base-class functions); the three attributes are now filled eagerly in __init__ so they shadow the lazy dispatch. Regression tests force equal size+mtime via os.utime so they fail on macOS too, not only on HAMMER2. Mutation-tested: both new tests fail with the fix disabled. Also corrected test_content_change_updates_dst, whose mtime assertion was itself granularity-dependent. 2089 passed on macOS 3.11.14 and DragonFly 3.11.12.

title: X5 Chroot: provision from two repos, keep /work/DeltaPorts unchanged
description:
The deepest coupling. Re-verified 2026-08-20 against the post-split tree; the
original notes were written pre-X8 and are corrected here.

WHAT BREAKS FIRST (not previously recorded): builder.py:154 validates the ports
tree by requiring a `dportsv3` file inside --delta-root ("Delta root does not
look like this repo") — a fossil from when the tool and the ports tree were one
checkout. X8 deleted DeltaPorts/dportsv3, so `dev-env create` now fails at
validation, before mirrors, chroot or venv. The venv failure described below is
unreachable until this is fixed.

THEN: dev-env clones exactly one repo to work/DeltaPorts (update.py:33-36
ENV_REPOS, builder.py:111), installs the generator venv from inside that
checkout (venv.py:24 requires work/DeltaPorts/scripts/generator/pyproject.toml,
venv.py:33 installs to .../.venv) and probes readiness with
/work/DeltaPorts/dportsv3 compose --help (venv.py:50, 72).

CORRECTION: hooks.py:50 is already fixed. X1 replaced the parents-walk with
package-local data in repo_hook_source(). Nothing to do there.

ALSO MISSING FROM THE ORIGINAL LIST:
- repos.py:13-27 RepoMirrors is a frozen 3-field dataclass with no slot for the
  tool repo; refresh_all() mirrors exactly 3 repos.
- state.py:24-25 SourceState has only delta_root — nowhere to record which tool
  checkout an env was built from.
- sync.py:15,91 GENERATOR_VENV_RELATIVE = scripts/generator/.venv, a dead path
  used to exclude the venv from git clean.
- builder.py:158-163 the dirty check and --allow-dirty cover only the ports
  checkout; post-split it is TOOL dirtiness that decides what reaches the chroot.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (unchanged): /work/DeltaPorts must keep meaning 'the ports
tree'. It is the agent's only legal edit surface — hardcoded in LLM prompt text
(prompts.py:146-360, tools.py:118) and enforced by guardrails that reject other
prefixes (worker.py:213, 251-258). The ports tree stays; the TOOL gets a second
path. cli.py:327,413,440,475 operate on the ports overlay and are correct as-is.

DESIGN AGREED:
- Tool repo reaches the chroot by mirroring the host polytropos checkout via the
  existing refresh_local_mirror, symmetric with delta_root. Keeps dev-env's
  purpose — testing local tool edits in a chroot — intact.
- In-chroot tool path is /work/polytropos (matches the repo name; avoids a
  second rename when dportsv3 -> polytropos lands).
- Host discovery: --tool-root, then $DPORTS_DEV_TOOL_ROOT, then raise —
  mirroring default_delta_root() at builder.py:226-252. bin/dportsv3 exports the
  variable; paths.py:31-34 already names the wrapper as the one component
  entitled to know repo layout, so no parents-walk enters a package.
- Venv cache key hashes BOTH pyproject.toml files. bin/dportsv3:193 notes the
  generator venv contains dev-env too, so hashing only the generator pyproject
  would silently reuse a stale venv when dev-env deps change.
- State schema 1 -> 2, hard cutover: fail loudly on schema 1 telling the operator
  to recreate. No migration — pre-split envs cannot work post-split anyway. The
  x6 2026Q3 reference chroot is expendable (confirmed with the operator).

REMAINING SURFACES: builder.py:110-114,154,158-163,195,200; venv.py:24,29,33,50,72;
repos.py:13-27; update.py:33-36; state.py:17-25; sync.py:15; helpers.py:28,30,69,
138,151-152,182; cli.py:27,35 (--delta-root help text is stale, add --tool-root);
dsynth-hooks/dportsv3-hooks.conf.example:36; bin/dportsv3 (export the variable).

OUT OF SCOPE, follow-up bead: sync-dirty for the tool repo. Resetting the tool
checkout invalidates the generator venv and needs a rebuild path; not in the
acceptance criteria.

TEST REALITY: builder.py, venv.py, repos.py, update.py and sync.py have no test
coverage — only 7 test files touch dports_dev_env and none of them these. A green
suite proves nothing here; criterion 5 on x6 is the real validation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. dev-env create provisions both repos into a chroot.
2. /work/DeltaPorts still resolves to the ports tree and every agent guardrail
   and prompt path is unchanged.
3. The generator venv is built from the tool repo, with a readiness probe that
   targets the new tool path.
4. In-chroot helpers, hook config and DELTAPORTS_ROOT are consistent with the
   new layout.
5. The tool runs end to end in a freshly provisioned chroot: compose and
   reapply from /work/polytropos against /work/DeltaPorts.

Criterion 5 originally read "a real agent job runs end to end". Narrowed
2026-08-21: that exercises the agentic loop, which needs services this repo has
no supported way to run — a separate gap, filed on its own, not something this
layout change owns or can be blocked on.
notes:
Criterion 5 run on x6 (DragonFly 6.5), 2026-08-20. Criteria 1-4 proven on real
hardware; the agent-job half of criterion 5 is NOT done.

PROVEN:
- create provisions both repos: /work/DeltaPorts and /work/polytropos side by
  side; the ports tree has ports/ and special/ and does NOT contain the tool.
- venv builds from the tool repo at /work/polytropos/.venv via the TOOL_BIN
  probe on first create, and restored from cache on the second — the key works
  across creates.
- compose in-chroot: applied=9544, which is exactly the with---lock-root
  baseline from 7ac5fb7 (the degraded path gives 9531). 136 errors, all ports
  content drift (patch conflicts, ambiguous _AR/_RANLIB), no layout errors.
- reapply editors/vim in-chroot: exit 0, cwd=/work/DeltaPorts, tool invoked
  from /work/polytropos.
- guardrails unchanged: worker.py still gates on /work/DeltaPorts/ports/.
- status reports both checkouts with branch/commit/dirty.
- schema-1 cutover: the pre-split 2026Q3 env read as invalid in list and
  destroy cleaned it via the partial-env path without stranding it.

FOUND AND FIXED, only visible by running it:
- 2c63825 initial_state() hardcoded schema=1, so every env was unreadable the
  moment it was saved. create never re-reads its own state, so it reported
  success and the next command failed. Test added.
- e17a8be showenv grepped ^DPORTS_ only, so neither source root appeared.

NOT DONE: "a real agent job runs end to end in a freshly provisioned chroot."
Needs the agentic LLM loop with credentials on x6; not attempted.

x6 state: env 2026Q3-editors_vim is ready. The checkout there carries an
uncommitted copy of builder.py/helpers.py matching 2c63825 and e17a8be, since
those are unpushed; a pull will clear it. Created with --allow-dirty for that
reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: X3 Prove the seam: run the tool from outside the ports repo
description: The go/no-go gate before touching git history. With X1+X2 done, the tool should already be able to operate on a ports tree it does not live in. Run compose, migration inventory, the tracker and the full test suite with the tool checked out at a path unrelated to the ports repo, pointing at DeltaPorts via the explicit delta_root. This is what proves the extraction is mechanical rather than a rewrite. Includes fixing the tests that reach across the boundary: test_hook_record_result_alignment.py (reads scripts/dsynth-hooks), test_decision_parity.py (reads config/), test_worker_guardrails.py + test_worker_hooks_disabled.py (parents[3] walks), and the 5 test_dev_env_*.py that import across packages.
acceptance_criteria: 1) compose --delta-root <ports repo> produces byte-identical output to running in-tree. 2) Full suite green with the tool outside the ports repo. 3) No test reaches out of the tool repo except through the configured delta_root. 4) Documented as the supported way to run the tool.
notes:
CRITERION 1 VERIFIED (2026-08-20, DragonFly x6.sector.int 6.5-DEVELOPMENT): compose from the extracted repo is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the in-tree tool.

METHOD. Two detached worktrees of DeltaPorts at 1f1ee8b9d3a (the last commit that still contained the toolchain; 75dee579255 is its child and removed it). Separate worktree per run because compose WRITES BACK into the delta root - each run mutated 31 files marking stale overlays removed_in - so a shared input would have silently corrupted run B.
  Run A (in-tree, pre-split): cd <worktreeA> && ./dportsv3 compose --target @2026Q3 --output out-intree --freebsd-root ~/s/freebsd-ports --lock-root ~/s/dports   (delta-root defaults to cwd)
  Run B (extracted repo):     cd ~/s/polytropos && ./bin/dportsv3 compose --target @2026Q3 --delta-root <worktreeB> --output out-newrepo --freebsd-root ~/s/freebsd-ports --lock-root ~/s/dports

CONTROLS. 'git diff 1f1ee8b9d3a 75dee579255 -- ports special' is EMPTY, so ports data is identical across the split; the deletion commit touched only tooling (386 scripts/, 43 docs/, 5 .claude/, 2 config/). Both runs used the same freebsd-ports (branch 2026Q3) and the same ~/s/dports lock root. The tool is therefore the only variable.

RESULT. diff -qr over both trees: 0 differences, exit 0. Entries 228979 = 228979. Path lists (find | sort) identical. files=180451 symlinks=0 dirs=48527 on both. Apparent bytes 587673075 = 587673075. 'du -sh' showed 335M vs 333M, which is HAMMER2 transparent compression, not content - apparent size is identical to the byte.
Comparison deliberately used diff -r, NOT the tool's own fsutils.diff_tree, which poly-mdx shows is broken.

SIDE RESULTS. (a) Both tools reported ops=9567 applied=9544 fallback=46 errors=134 with the same breakdown (E_COMPOSE_COMPAT_FAILED=32, E_COMPOSE_STALE_OVERLAY=31, E_COMPOSE_APPLY_FAILED=3), so the 134 compose errors are PRE-EXISTING ports drift, not extraction damage. (b) The extracted tool resolved config from polytropos/config via DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR while the in-tree tool used DeltaPorts/config - different config dirs, identical output.

CRITERION 3 ALSO VERIFIED: full suite run on x6 with DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT UNSET gives the same 2082 passed / 3 failed as with it set, so no test depends on the ports repo. Remaining parents[N] walks in tests are parents[1] = tool repo root, which does not leave the tool repo.

STILL OPEN: criterion 2 (3 failures, all poly-mdx, a pre-existing filecmp bug that reproduces on macOS too - not an extraction regression) and criterion 4 (poly-3ze). See also poly-170 for the DragonFly dev-install blocker.

ARTIFACTS left in place on x6 for re-running after poly-mdx: ~/x3-parity/{DeltaPorts-presplit,DeltaPorts-forB,out-intree,out-newrepo} (~1.6G) plus two worktree registrations in ~/s/DeltaPorts/.git/worktrees/. Remove with 'git -C ~/s/DeltaPorts worktree remove' x2 and rm -rf ~/x3-parity.
close_reason: Closed

title: X2 Break the bidirectional generator<->dev-env sys.path bridge
description: The two distributions import each other at runtime by mutating sys.path, with no declared dependency either way. Verified: env_resolver.py:52-62 inserts parents[3]/tools/dev-env and imports dports_dev_env.config/store; cli.py:884 (dev-env) inserts parents[3]/generator and imports dportsv3.agent.health; health.py:45 reads the dev-env's runtime-profiles.toml. All three assume generator/ and tools/dev-env/ are siblings under one scripts/ dir — which is exactly what extraction changes. pyproject files also cross-pin jsonschema by hand-written comment rather than a real dependency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No sys.path mutation between the two packages. 2) The dependency direction is declared and acyclic (either dev-env depends on the generator, or the shared piece — env resolution / runtime profiles — moves to a package both can import). 3) jsonschema pinning is expressed once, not duplicated in a comment. 4) Each package imports cleanly with the other absent.
close_reason: Declared dportsv3 -> dports-dev-env, acyclic. Reverse edge (dev-env health CLI shim) moved to 'dportsv3 env-health'. Manifest moved into the package, ships in a wheel. jsonschema pin dropped from both (dead in code). Suite 53 -> 11 failures; remainder is X1. Commit fdba90e in ~/s/polytropos.

title: X1 De-couple path discovery (in place, repo still works)
description:
Do this BEFORE any file moves — it is the bulk of the work and is independently valuable. Every place the tool finds something by walking out of its own directory must take an explicit, configured path instead. Verified sites: runner.py:89 + _manual_test_triage_tier.py:182 (parents[4]/config -> agentic-policy.json), delivery/config.py:258 (delivery.token), delivery/orchestrator.py:92 (delivery.toml), snippets.py:15 (scripts/snippet-extractor), worker.py:52 + verify_fix.py:132 (parents[4]/dportsv3 wrapper), health.py:45 (parents[3]/tools/dev-env/runtime-profiles.toml), playbooks.py:345 (ancestor walk for docs/agent-playbooks), cli.py:60/210/235/261/370 (--delta-root defaults to Path('.')), builder.py:225 default_delta_root()=parents[4].

playbooks.py is the dangerous one: it returns None on failure, so after a move the agent silently loses all pattern knowledge with no error. Every one of these must fail LOUDLY or be explicitly configured.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single documented resolution order per input (CLI flag > env var > config > packaged default), no parents[N] walking out of the package. 2) delta_root (the ports tree) is explicit — never Path('.') by accident. 3) Missing playbooks/policy/config raises or logs a clear error; nothing degrades silently. 4) Tool data that is really tool-owned (agent-playbooks, dops_quickref.md) ships as package data. 5) Suite green with the repo unmoved.
close_reason: Single resolver dportsv3/paths.py. Tool-owned data (playbooks, config templates, dsynth hooks, snippet extractor) moved into the packages; site-owned inputs named via env/flag. All raise instead of returning None. Verified via non-editable wheel install resolving everything from /. Suite 2085 passed, zero parents[N] walks left. Commit df9a668.

title: Worklist has no landing place for issues knocked off the happy path
description:
The issue worklist (/agentic, build_issue_worklist) silently loses or mislabels issues that leave the accept->deliver happy path. Two verified cases, one root cause: issue_bucket derives the band from the ACTIONABLE OCCURRENCE's resolution, so anything that changes the issue without changing its bundle (or blanks the bundle) lands wrong.

CASE 1 — red confirm build still reads 'Awaiting delivery'. reopen_issue_build_failed sets state='unresolved' and nulls delivery_bundle_id but does NOT touch the bundle, whose resolution stays 'accepted'. issue_bucket falls through and returns 'delivering' for occ_key=='accepted'. So a red confirm moves the issue from one looks-fixed band (resolving) to another (awaiting delivery) instead of 'decide'. A3's stated goal — stop an unfixed issue looking as good as fixed — is defeated. The only real signal is manual_handoff.md on a bundle the operator has no reason to open.

CASE 2 — operator bundle-reopen makes the issue VANISH. Reopening a bundle sets bundles.resolution to NULL -> fix_state.fix_status = 'unknown' -> worklist_bucket = None -> issue_bucket returns None -> build_issue_worklist DROPS it (issue_state.py:257-258, 'Issues that aren't operator-actionable right now (bucket None) are omitted'). The issue disappears from /agentic entirely and is only findable on /agentic/issues. Bucket None means 'the runner is working it, nothing to do yet', which is exactly wrong for an issue an operator just reopened by hand.

Reproduced live on the demo DB: iss-queued and iss-redconfirm both sat at bucket=None and were absent from the dashboard worklist while still listed on /agentic/issues. Confirmed via the events audit log that the state writes themselves were all correct — this is purely a projection/UX hole, not state corruption.

Compounding UX factor: there are two different Reopen buttons (bundle-level and issue-level) whose effects differ (bundle reopen never changes issue state), with nothing in the UI explaining which one moves what.
acceptance_criteria: 1) An issue whose confirm build went red lands in an actionable band (decide), not delivering. 2) An issue whose bundle an operator reopened stays VISIBLE in the worklist in an actionable band, instead of being dropped by the bucket-None rule. 3) Decide whether the bundle's resolution should move off 'accepted' when its confirm build fails. 4) Bucket None is reserved for genuinely runner-owned work; operator-touched issues never fall into it. 5) The red verdict + handoff are reachable from the issue, not only from the bundle artifact. 6) The two Reopen actions are distinguishable in the UI (what each one moves). 7) Tests pin the bucket for (a) reopened-by-red-confirm and (b) operator-reopened bundle.
close_reason: Fixed: unknown -> decide (bucket None now reserved for runner-owned work), and accepted-occurrence-on-open-issue -> decide (stale pre-resolving branch). Plus 'confirming' added to _INFLIGHT_JOB_STATES. Demo worklist 4/8 -> 8/8.

title: Confirm loop: duplicate builds on restart / lock contention / multi-runner
description: Adversarial review found 3 verified double-enqueue paths, each costing a full dsynth build. (a) RESTART: _reset_building_markers clears every building_generation at startup, but a confirm job sitting in pending/ SURVIVES — reap_orphans deliberately leaves QUEUED claimable (lifecycle.py:476 'QUEUED stays queued') and reap_stale_queued only reaps rows whose .job file is missing. So the old job is still claimable AND the feed enqueues a fresh one: two builds, two greens, and with the A4 threshold of 2 the issue resolves on what was effectively one requested confirmation. (b) NON-ATOMIC MARK: process_build_requests enqueues the job file and only then calls _mark_issue_building, which swallows sqlite3.Error and returns silently when the conn is None. If the tracker holds the write lock past busy_timeout the marker is never set, nothing is logged, and the next loop pass (<=5s) enqueues a duplicate. (c) MULTI-RUNNER: a second runner's startup sweep wipes the first runner's live in-flight markers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A queued-but-unclaimed confirm job is reconciled on restart rather than duplicated (reap it, or make the marker sweep aware of pending confirm jobs). 2) Enqueue+mark is atomic, or the mark failing prevents/undoes the enqueue and is logged. 3) Multi-runner startup does not clear another live runner's markers. 4) Tests cover all three.
close_reason: Fixed the two in-scope paths: claim-before-enqueue (CAS, failed claim never enqueues) and coherent restart sweep (discard queued confirm jobs + clear markers, then re-derive). Multi-runner filed separately as a pre-existing system-wide gap.

title: Confirm loop: issue stuck in resolving on permanently-doomed builds
description: A machinery gave-up deliberately leaves building_generation set to avoid hot-looping a broken env, and ONLY the startup _reset_building_markers clears it. Consequences verified: (a) a long-lived runner parks the issue in resolving forever with no retry, no backoff and no operator-visible signal beyond one activity row; recovery requires a human restarting the runner, which is documented nowhere operator-facing. (b) PERMANENTLY-DOOMED builds loop: run_verify_fix raises VerifyFixError when the bundle has no changes.diff or it is empty (verify_fix.py:206-215), and the dispatch raises when no dev-env is available — so every restart clears the marker, re-enqueues, raises again, re-sets the marker. The issue never leaves resolving and each restart burns a job. Operator escape hatch does exist (manual resolve/reopen are allowed from resolving, issue_state.py:59-60) but is undiscoverable. Overlaps C4 (per-key backoff).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A doomed confirm (missing/empty changes.diff, no dev-env) is detected and does not retry indefinitely — terminal state + operator signal. 2) A stalled in-flight marker is recoverable without a runner restart. 3) The operator can see WHY an issue is parked in resolving. 4) Coordinate with C4 backoff so the two do not conflict.
close_reason: Fixed: machinery failures now clear the marker and retry without a restart, bounded by DP_CONFIRM_MAX_FAILURES (default 3), after which the issue is reopened with a manual handoff. Pacing (per-key backoff) remains C4.

title: A2 Green -> resolved (build-confirmed) + Green Head
description: A2 Green -> resolved (build-confirmed). On a green confirm build, advance the issue resolving->resolved and record the Green-Head build ordinal per (target,origin). Read-only on build_* (reads port_status).
design:
## Design

On a GREEN confirm-build verdict (from A1's report-back), make the build — not the
merge — the authority that resolves the issue.

**Transition:** in the confirm-build report-back handler, when verdict=green for the
issue currently in `resolving`:
- `state: resolving -> resolved`, `resolved_at = now`, source `'build-confirmed'`
  (reuse the `resolve_issue` writer, issue_actions.py:83, or an inline UPDATE with
  the same shape/event).
- GUARD: only from `state='resolving'` (mirror `mark_issue_resolving`'s
  `WHERE state IN (...)`, issue_actions.py:112) so a muted / unresolved / already-
  resolved issue is untouched.
- advance `last_confirmed_build_generation = generation`, clear `building_generation`.

**Green Head:** record the build ordinal at which (target, origin) went green — from
`port_status.last_success_run_id` / `build_runs.id` (schema.py:384/355). Store it as
`green_head_run_id` on the issue (new column) or a small `issue_green_head` side
row. This is the "known-good boundary" C3 derives `regressed` against (a later build
re-emitting the fingerprint at an ordinal > green head = regression).

**Authority shift (the point of the feature):** today `delivery_sync.py:148`
(`set_bundle_merged_resolution`) flips `resolved` on PR merge. A2 moves that
authority to the green build. For the MVP, merge becomes an OBSERVATION that no
longer directly resolves; the clean two-axis split (resolution vs build-observation)
is C3. Keep the change minimal here — do not delete the merge path yet, just stop
treating merge as the resolve trigger for issues that went through `resolving`.

**Emits** `issue_resolved` with `source='build-confirmed'` + `green_head_run_id`.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Green verdict for a resolving issue -> state resolving->resolved, resolved_at set, source=build-confirmed, event emitted. 2) Guard: transition only from state=resolving (muted/unresolved/resolved untouched). 3) Green-Head ordinal per (target,origin) recorded (green_head_run_id from port_status.last_success_run_id/build_runs.id). 4) last_confirmed_build_generation advanced, building_generation cleared (no re-enqueue). 5) Merge no longer directly flips resolved for issues that went through resolving (authority moves to the build; full split is C3; merge path not deleted yet). 6) Test: resolving+green -> resolved w/ green-head; muted+green -> untouched.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed + committed. Green head implemented as a build_runs watermark (not port_status.last_success_run_id) because dsynth hooks are disabled in the dev-env so confirm builds never reach build_runs/port_status.

title: C1 Build intent (generation counter / build_requests)
description: C1 Build intent. The resolving transition writes desired build state — a generation counter on the issue (requested_build_generation) or a build_requests row. Crash-safe, self-dedup. Prior art: K8s observedGeneration.
design:
## Design

Record *desired build state* on the issue row when a fix is accepted, as a
monotonic generation counter — the level-triggered spine (K8s observedGeneration),
NOT an edge-triggered command.

**Schema (db/schema.py, `issues` table):**
- add `requested_build_generation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
- add `last_confirmed_build_generation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
- add `building_generation INTEGER` (NULL = no build in flight; single-flight marker, set by C2)

**Write point — `mark_issue_resolving` (tracker/routes/issue_actions.py:98):**
Extend the existing single UPDATE (the one that sets `state='resolving'`,
`delivery_bundle_id`) to also bump `requested_build_generation =
requested_build_generation + 1`, in the SAME statement / same txn. This is the
"record intent" half of the verify_requests pattern (agentic_api.py:533), but on
the issue row itself rather than an append table — so it is level-triggered and
self-dedups (a re-accept just bumps the counter; no duplicate queue rows — that is
C2's job).

**Read feed for C2:** a query helper (tracker/agentic_queries/issues.py) returning
issues where `state='resolving' AND requested_build_generation >
last_confirmed_build_generation AND (building_generation IS NULL OR
building_generation < requested_build_generation)`.

**Event:** extend the emitted `issue_resolving` event (issue_actions.py:117) to
carry `requested_build_generation`, or emit a companion `issue_build_requested`.

**Rejected alternative:** a `build_requests` append table mirroring verify_requests
exactly. Rejected because it is edge-triggered — it can drift (a request row says
done while state later regresses) and needs its own dedup. The counter-on-issue is
crash-safe by construction (one row, one UPDATE) and is what C2/A2 compare against.

**Why crash-safe:** the generation bump rides the same single UPDATE as the state
write, under the caller's BEGIN IMMEDIATE txn — a crash leaves either the old or the
new generation, never a half-written intent.
acceptance_criteria: 1) issues table gains requested_build_generation, last_confirmed_build_generation, building_generation. 2) mark_issue_resolving bumps requested_build_generation +1 in the same UPDATE that sets state=resolving (one statement, same txn). 3) Emits an event carrying the new generation. 4) A read helper returns issues where state=resolving AND requested>confirmed AND not in-flight. 5) Test: accept -> gen=1/state=resolving; re-accept newer bundle -> gen=2; crash between leaves old-or-new gen, never half.
close_reason: Implemented + unit-verified; committed 7eaa21a2624 (C1/C2) and d75906b8877 (A1 + C2 go-live). Real build path needs a live chroot to exercise.

title: Block C — Reconcile seam: level-triggered build trigger
description: Wire the build-trigger as level-triggered intent, not a command. The resolving transition writes desired state; the runner re-derives 'does a build need to exist?' each loop and stays sole queue writer. Same shape as verify_requests; tracker never touches the queue filesystem. Prior art: Kubernetes controllers, ArgoCD, Sentry.

title: A1 Confirm-build execution
description: A1 Confirm-build execution — build (target,origin) with the accepted fix and report green/red, via a runner-dispatched job reusing dev-env apply-and-build / dsynth build. Cleaner once the build runs on Block B isolated worktree substrate (sequencing is a preference, not a hard dep).
design:
## Design

Execute the confirm-build and report a green/red verdict, REUSING the existing
in-process build-and-report machinery — no new build engine.

**Enqueue + dispatch:**
- `enqueue_confirm_build_job(queue_root, *, issue_key, bundle_id, origin, target,
  generation, env, requested_by)` — mirror `enqueue_verify_job` (runner.py:1850);
  new job `type=confirm`, carries `issue_key` + `generation` so the verdict can be
  tied back to the exact C1 intent.
- Runner dispatch arm handles `type=confirm` by calling
  `dportsv3.verify_fix.run_verify_fix` in-process (same path the verify job uses) —
  it applies the accepted fix (the `delivery_bundle_id` diff) and drives dev-env
  `apply-and-build` → dsynth build for (target, origin).

**Verdict source (dsynth-owned, read-only):** the build reports through the
existing hook path into `build_results` / `port_status` (schema.py:367/378) — we do
NOT write those core columns ourselves (the "dsynth owns build data" constraint).
Read `port_status.last_attempt_result` / `last_success_run_id` for the verdict, or
capture run_verify_fix's returned status.

**Report-back:** POST the verdict to a new tracker endpoint (mirror verify's
`POST /api/bundles/{id}/verification`), carrying `(issue_key, generation, verdict,
build_run_id)`. That endpoint hands off to A2 (green) / A3 (red).

**Generation bookkeeping:** whatever the outcome, set
`last_confirmed_build_generation = generation` and clear `building_generation` — so
the C2 loop stops re-enqueuing this generation. (A2 additionally resolves on green;
A3 reopens on red.)

**Block B note:** runs correctly on today's shared checkout; cleaner/safer on the
Block B per-job worktree substrate, but that is a preference, not a hard dependency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) enqueue_confirm_build_job + a type=confirm dispatch handler that runs the accepted fix through verify_fix.run_verify_fix (reused, no new build engine) for (target,origin). 2) Produces a structured green/red verdict tied to (issue_key, generation, target, origin, build_run_id). 3) Reads port_status read-only; does NOT write dsynth-owned build_* core columns. 4) Verdict POSTs back to a new tracker endpoint that routes to A2/A3. 5) Regardless of outcome, sets last_confirmed_build_generation=generation and clears building_generation. 6) Test: stubbed green -> verdict green vs generation; stubbed red -> verdict red.
close_reason: Implemented + unit-verified; committed 7eaa21a2624 (C1/C2) and d75906b8877 (A1 + C2 go-live). Real build path needs a live chroot to exercise.

title: C2 Runner reconcile loop (level-triggered)
description: C2 Runner reconcile loop (level-triggered). Each loop, re-derive needs-a-build (requested_gen > last_built_gen) and enqueue a confirm-build job; runner is sole queue writer. Mirrors process_verify_requests. Prior art: K8s level-triggered reconcile + resync.
design:
## Design

New `process_build_requests(queue_root)` in agent/runner.py, a near-clone of
`process_verify_requests` (runner.py:880), called from the main loop right next to
it (runner.py:3831). Level-triggered: each pass RE-DERIVES which issues need a build
rather than draining a command queue.

**Each pass:**
1. SELECT the C1 feed — issues with `state='resolving' AND
   requested_build_generation > last_confirmed_build_generation` and not already
   in flight (`building_generation IS NULL OR < requested_build_generation`).
2. For each, look up `delivery_bundle_id` → its origin/target (mirror the bundle
   lookup at runner.py:919).
3. Call a new `enqueue_confirm_build_job(...)` (mirror `enqueue_verify_job`,
   runner.py:1850; new job `type=confirm`).
4. Single-flight mark: set `building_generation = requested_build_generation` for
   that issue (mirror `_mark_verify_request`, runner.py:953) so the next loop pass
   does NOT re-enqueue while the build runs. A1/A2 clear/advance it on completion.

**Invariants preserved:**
- Runner is the SOLE writer to the queue filesystem; the tracker only wrote the
  intent counter (C1). Restores the tracker-is-read-only-for-queue rule, same as
  verify_requests.
- Env selection reuses `env_resolver` (per-job dev-env precedence).

**'env busy' vs real failure (MVP):** if no env is free, skip and retry next loop
(no penalty, no in-flight mark). Per-key exponential backoff for *real* failures is
C4 — not needed for the MVP.

**Resync:** because it re-derives from the counter every pass, a lost enqueue or a
runner restart self-heals — the issue still shows requested > confirmed next loop.
acceptance_criteria: 1) process_build_requests(queue_root) added, called from the runner main loop next to process_verify_requests. 2) Each pass re-derives issues needing a build (requested>confirmed, state=resolving, not in-flight) and enqueues one confirm-build job per (target,origin,delivery_bundle_id) via enqueue_confirm_build_job. 3) Runner is the sole queue-fs writer; tracker wrote only the counter. 4) Single-flight: two loop passes before the build finishes enqueue exactly ONE job (building_generation marker). 5) env-busy -> skip/retry next loop, no penalty, no in-flight mark. 6) Test: seeded resolving issue -> one job; second pass -> none.
notes: Mechanism implemented + smoke-verified (enqueue_confirm_build_job, process_build_requests, _mark_issue_building single-flight, _reset_building_markers crash-recovery). NOT wired into the runner main loop yet: the loop call + _reset_building_markers startup call land WITH A1 (DeltaPorts-rk0), because C1 already creates resolving issues and a type=confirm job has no dispatch handler until A1. Producer+consumer go live atomically. Confirm-specific lifecycle transitions (CONFIRM_START/GREEN/RED) are A1's.
close_reason: Implemented + unit-verified; committed 7eaa21a2624 (C1/C2) and d75906b8877 (A1 + C2 go-live). Real build path needs a live chroot to exercise.

title: Block A — Execution oracle: gate `resolved` on a build, not the merge
description: Stop trusting the PR-merge event; make `resolved` mean the port actually builds. Reuses verify_fix.py build-and-report machinery; reads dsynth-owned port_status read-only; joins on (target,origin,fingerprint). Prior art: ClusterFuzz progression, SWE-bench, Google TAP.

title: Cross-env dependency hazard: divergent ports trees produce conflicting fixes
description:
REGISTERED AND DEFERRED — genuinely complicated, needs its own design pass. Blocks the epic; do not build multi-env scheduling without an answer here, even if the answer is 'serialize dependent origins'.

THE HAZARD: each env has its own DeltaPorts checkout, so the trees diverge. If A depends on B and you fix B in env2, that fix is invisible to env1. A then rebuilds against unfixed B, fails for a reason that is already solved, and the agent in env1 tries to fix B itself. Two agents then edit the same port in two divergent trees and someone reconciles the conflicting patches later.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT TODAY: there is no dependency awareness anywhere in dportsv3 — no BUILD_DEPENDS/RUN_DEPENDS parsing, no dep graph, nothing (grepped). _has_active_same_origin_job (runner.py:1418) guards a single origin, not a dependency cone, so it does not help.

WHERE THE DATA COULD COME FROM: dsynth already computes the graph to order its own builds. We just never capture it. Also available from make -V BUILD_DEPENDS per port. Cheap sources exist; the hard part is the scheduling policy, not the data.

SKETCH OF OPTIONS, none chosen: partition work by dependency cone so one env owns a whole cone; or give each env an exclusive origin set (lanes); or allow overlap and detect collisions after the fact at merge.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A design exists for how concurrent envs avoid working inside one dependency cone. 2. The chosen policy is implemented or explicitly deferred with the hazard documented where a scheduler author will see it.

title: Scope the dsynth busy-gate to an env instead of the whole host
description:
dsynth_active (runner.py:2169) pgreps -x dsynth host-wide and returns busy if ANY dsynth exists. Called from _gate_blocked (runner.py:4525) it pauses the entire runner loop, so one build anywhere blocks every env. Needed for multi-env; also correct single-env.

REJECTED APPROACH — matching the dsynth profile on argv. Looks attractive because DPORTS_DSYNTH_PROFILE is per-env (dsynth.py:11) and appears as -p on every invocation from worker.py:2143 and the dev-env helpers. Two reasons it does not hold:

  * sanitize_name is not injective. It maps / : @ and space all to _ and deletes anything else, so envs 'foo/bar', 'foo:bar', 'foo\@bar', 'foo bar' and 'foo_bar' share ONE profile name. Attribution would point at the wrong env.
  * dsynth.ini sets profile_selected=, so an operator typing 'dsynth build x11/foo' inside the chroot passes no -p at all. argv shows nothing and the env reads free while a build runs — exactly the operator-initiated case the host-wide pgrep exists to catch.

CANDIDATE APPROACH — attribute by filesystem, not by process. dsynth's buildbase is per-env (/work/dsynth/build) and mounts_under() already exists (dev-env/dports_dev_env/mounts.py:58), reading the host mount table by path. Builder mounts under an env's buildbase are ground truth regardless of who started dsynth. MUST VERIFY ON A REAL HOST FIRST: that dsynth actually mounts under buildbase, and how wide the window is between process start and first mount. Not asserted.

DESIGN RULE: failure to attribute must mean BUSY, not free. Keep the host-wide pgrep as the floor and let attribution only ever narrow it.

RELATED WART: dsynth_active currently fails OPEN when pgrep is missing (runner.py:2199 returns False), which is the wrong direction under that rule.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A dsynth running in env A does not gate env B. 2. An operator-started dsynth (no -p on argv) still gates its own env. 3. Unattributable dsynth gates everything. 4. Missing pgrep fails closed, not open.

title: (EPIC) Multi-env concurrent building
description:
Run builds in more than one dev-env at once. The chroot layer is already close: each env root is a read-only nullfs of a shared provisioned base plus per-env writable dirs (runtime.py:76), and every dsynth path is inside the env — Directory_packages, buildbase, logs, options all under /work/dsynth (dsynth.py:44-52). env_health_status is already keyed by env and resolve_env_for_job already takes env per job.

The blockers are all in the runner's scheduling layer:

1. dsynth_active pgreps host-wide and gates the WHOLE loop from _gate_blocked (runner.py:4525), not per job. Any dsynth anywhere pauses everything.
2. The runner loop is serial: one claim -> process_job at a time, no pool.
3. Env resolution is a preference, not a scheduler. Precedence is job.dev_env > tracker_active_env (singleton) > --env > auto-pick-if-exactly-one > refuse. With >1 env and no operator selection it REFUSES (env_resolver.py:127), so a second env degrades the system rather than scaling it.
4. jobs has no env column; the env lives only in the .job payload.

THE FORK IN THE ROAD: in-process worker pool vs multiple runner processes. A pool sidesteps the lease/liveness problem entirely — one process owning N envs needs no cross-process ownership protocol. Multiple runners needs the full runner-identity + lease machinery (poly-bg1). Decide this before building anything under this epic.

Not a blocker, checked and dismissed: /usr/distfiles is bind-mounted RW into every env (runtime.py:94), but ports checksum distfiles, so a raced or partial fetch fails its checksum rather than being silently consumed.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The pool-vs-multiple-runners decision is made and recorded. 2. Two envs can build concurrently without either corrupting the other or falsely gating each other. 3. The cross-env dependency hazard has an explicit answer (see child bead), even if that answer is 'serialize dependent origins'.

title: No supported way to run the services
description:
The tracker, artifact-store and agent-queue-runner have no documented,
repeatable way to be brought up. The operator runs them from an ad-hoc local
script that is not in the repo, so nobody else can start the stack and nothing
that depends on it can be exercised or tested.

Surfaced while scoping X5's criterion 5: "a real agent job runs end to end"
could not be attempted, and the reason turned out to be this, not anything
about the chroot layout. Criterion 5 was narrowed to what X5 owns and this was
split out.

TODO before picking this up: capture what the operator's script actually
starts, in what order, with what environment (litellm provider config —
DeepSeek, not Claude — ports, queue/log roots, tracker DB). Ask rather than
reconstruct; guessing produces a runbook that does not match the working setup.

docs/OPERATOR_SETUP.md covers per-command invocation but not bringing the stack
up as a unit.

title: sudo dev-env runs leave root-owned files in the user's venv
description:
dev-env commands need root, and bin/dportsv3 reinstalls dev-env into the venv
whenever its sources change. So `sudo bin/dportsv3 dev-env ...` after any
dev-env edit writes root-owned files into the developer's checkout — seen on
x6: 10 root-owned files under dev-env/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages after
one `sudo dev-env list`.

The next unprivileged run then fails to reinstall, and the usual reflex (run it
under sudo again) entrenches it.

Known workaround is "bootstrap unprivileged first", but that only covers venv
creation, not the reinstall-on-source-change path, which recurs every edit.

Options: have the wrapper drop privileges for the pip step, keep the dev-env
venv outside the checkout, or refuse to bootstrap as root with a clear message.

title: polytropos has no CI at all
description:
Neither repository runs CI against this tool. Found while verifying X6: the
Jenkinsfile its criterion 1 was written against was never tracked in git — an
uncommitted local draft in the DeltaPorts working copy, since deleted at the
operator's instruction. Polytropos has no Jenkinsfile and no .github/workflows.
DeltaPorts' .github/workflows/github-actions-pullrequests.yml shells
/root/bin/*.sh on a self-hosted runner and does not touch dportsv3, so it is a
consumer of ports/ only and is unaffected either way.

The suite is 2089 tests and runs green on macOS (3.11.14) and DragonFly
(3.11.12), so there is something worth gating on. Nothing gates on it.

Worth deciding before this is picked up:
- what runs it — GitHub Actions on the polytropos repo is the obvious default,
  but the tool's real target is DragonFly, which needs a self-hosted runner
- whether a macOS/Linux run of the pure-Python suite is enough for PR gating,
  with DragonFly reserved for the chroot/dev-env paths that cannot run
  anywhere else
- poly-170 blocks installing the [dev] extra on DragonFly (maturin needs
  rustc >= 1.89, pkg ships 1.85.1), so a DragonFly job cannot install pytest
  the normal way today

title: sync-dirty does not propagate host tool-repo edits into an env
description:
After X5 a chroot holds two checkouts: the ports tree at /work/DeltaPorts and
the tool at /work/polytropos. `dev-env sync-dirty` (sync.py DirtySyncer) only
resets and patches the ports checkout, so uncommitted TOOL edits on the host
never reach a running env — you have to destroy and recreate to test a tool
change, which is the workflow dev-env exists to avoid.

Deliberately left out of X5: resetting the tool checkout invalidates the cached
generator venv (venv.py keys on pyproject hashes), so this needs a
rebuild-or-revalidate path rather than a straight `git reset --hard` + patch.

Was flagged during the X5 review and confirmed as a real gap, not dismissed.

title: [dev] and [tracker] extras cannot install on DragonFly: maturin needs rustc >= 1.89, base has 1.85.1
description: The documented build recipe in CLAUDE.md ('uv pip install --python .venv -e ".[tracker,agent,dev]"') cannot complete on DragonFly, for two independent reasons. (1) uv is not present on the DragonFly host (x6, DragonFly 6.5-DEVELOPMENT) and is not in pkg; bin/dportsv3 does not need it - the wrapper bootstraps with stock 'python3 -m venv' + 'pip install -e' (bin/dportsv3:167,170) - but the documented dev recipe assumes uv. (2) DragonFly is not a wheel platform, so pip builds sdists from source. mypy 2.3.1 now depends on librt>=0.13.0 and ast-serialize>=0.6.0, whose build backend is maturin; maturin 1.14.1 requires rustc 1.89 while pkg rust is 1.85.1, so the build dies with 'rustc 1.85.1 is not supported by the following packages' (also cargo-platform 1.88, icu_* 1.86, time 1.88, zip 1.88). [tracker] fails the same way via fastapi -> pydantic-core. Observed effect: 'pip install -e ".[dev]"' and '".[tracker,agent,dev]"' both fail. Workaround used to run the suite on x6: 'pip install pytest' alone (pure Python). The suite still collected all 2085 tests ONLY because fastapi 0.115.12 and litellm 1.65.0 happen to be installed system-wide in /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages and are visible to the venv - on a clean DragonFly box collection would fail. mypy is therefore not installable on the target platform at all, so type-checking cannot run there.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented dev setup that completes on a clean DragonFly host - e.g. pin mypy<2.3 (last release before the Rust-backed librt/ast-serialize deps), or split type-checking into an extra that is not required to run tests. 2) The suite installs and runs without relying on packages that happen to be present system-wide. 3) CLAUDE.md build instructions work on DragonFly as written, or state the platform caveat and the supported alternative explicitly.

title: compose needs three roots; --lock-root degrades silently and only --delta-root is documented
description: Running compose from outside the ports repo needs THREE input trees, but the docs name one. Verified on x6: --target and --output and --freebsd-root are mandatory, --delta-root defaults to $DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT else cwd, and --lock-root falls back to delta_root/'locked' (compose.py:98). DeltaPorts has no locked/ directory, so the fallback silently mis-resolves and yields 5x E_COMPOSE_LOCK_SOURCE_MISSING instead of naming the missing input. Passing --lock-root ~/s/dports (the DPorts checkout, per worker.py:304 'lock root (/work/DPorts/)') dropped errors 150 -> 134 and RAISED applied ops 9531 -> 9544, so the fallback was also losing real work. CLAUDE.md documents only --delta-root / $DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT. Silent degradation on a missing input is exactly what the paths.py invariant forbids - missing inputs must raise, not degrade.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A missing/unresolvable lock source raises a clear error naming the input instead of falling back to a path that does not exist. 2) Docs state the full three-root invocation (--delta-root, --freebsd-root, --lock-root) as the supported way to run outside the ports repo, satisfying X3 criterion 4. 3) Env-var equivalents documented alongside $DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT if they exist.
notes: Hash correction: the fix commit is 82329b8 (referenced as d1344fc before the attribution trailer was stripped and the unpushed commits rewritten).
close_reason: Fixed in d1344fc. A missing lock root is now reported once as E_COMPOSE_LOCK_ROOT_MISSING naming the path tried, and surfaced as a hint so it reaches plain compose output rather than only the JSON report. Gated on a type lock overlay actually needing the tree, preserving the documented 'only needed if' contract. Three-root invocation documented in CLAUDE.md and docs/dportsv3-user-guide.md, including that only --delta-root has an env var. Verified against the real DeltaPorts tree on x6. Satisfies X3 criterion 4.

title: X8 Cut over: delete moved files from the ports repo
description: The irreversible step, deliberately last and deliberately separate. Until this runs, both repos have the tool and the ports repo keeps working exactly as today, so every earlier phase is reversible. Remove scripts/generator, scripts/tools/dev-env, scripts/dsynth-hooks, scripts/snippet-extractor, the shims, the root ./dportsv3 wrapper, config/*.sample and the tool docs from the ports repo; leave ports/, special/, the ports-infra scripts and the legacy workflow. Keep a short pointer in the ports README saying where the tooling now lives and how to get it. Requires X1-X7 done and a green CI run against the split.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ports repo builds ports with no tool code present. 2) A pointer to the tool repo exists where contributors will look. 3) CI green from a clean checkout of both repos. 4) Tagged commit on both sides marking the split, so the boundary is findable later.
notes:
Re-reviewed 2026-08-21.
- Criterion 1 met: DeltaPorts builds ports with no tool code.
- Criterion 2 met: README.md, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md all name Polytropos. No
  URL in the pointer; not worth a bead.
- Criterion 3 has no subject: there is no CI on either side. See poly-1h4.
- Criterion 4: polytropos has no tag and does not need one — its root commit
  3414779 IS the split boundary, since the repo starts at the extraction.
  DeltaPorts' side is 75dee579255. Considered satisfied by construction.

title: X7 Move the beads issue history to the tool repo
description:
The issue tracker for the TOOLING lives in the ports repo: .beads/config.yaml pins sync.remote to git+https://github.com/dragonflybsd/deltaports.git, and the Dolt DB (.beads/embeddeddolt) plus interactions.jsonl sit under the ports checkout. Every open issue there — this epic included, plus the whole build-confirmed resolution programme (Blocks A-D) and the review findings — is tool work, not ports work. Also .beads/hooks/ installs post-checkout/post-merge/pre-commit/pre-push/prepare-commit-msg git hooks into whichever repo hosts it.

Decide and execute: move the Dolt DB to the tool repo and repoint sync.remote, versus leaving history behind and starting clean. Moving keeps the audit trail of why the design is what it is, which is the main asset here. Sequence this LAST — the beads DB is how the rest of this plan is tracked, so moving it mid-flight would be self-defeating.

Removed from DeltaPorts along with the managed CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md blocks. Commits 35539ae (poly) / fcc0be9f842 (DeltaPorts).

title: X6 Update the consumers: CI, hooks, docs, agent configs
description:
Consumers of the tool outside the tool itself. Re-verified 2026-08-20 from the
polytropos side; the original notes were written from the DeltaPorts side
before the cutover and three of the four criteria turned out to have no
subject at all.

CRITERION 1 (CI): NO SUBJECT. The Jenkinsfile that DEV_ENV_RUNNER='./dportsv3'
came from was never tracked in git — no history in either repository, in any
branch. It was an uncommitted local draft in the DeltaPorts working copy.
Deleted at the operator's instruction. Neither repo has any other CI: no
Jenkinsfile, no .github/workflows in polytropos. Filed separately as the
absence of CI is a real gap, just not this one.

CRITERION 2 (hooks reach the tool through a documented, configurable binary

title: Operator build controls: trigger / retry / cancel a confirm build
description:
The 'operable builds' requirement: an operator looking at an issue awaiting build confirmation has NO action available. The occurrence card offers only Reopen (correct for an accepted bundle) and the issue offers Resolve/Reopen — nothing to run, retry, or stop the confirm build itself.

The plumbing already exists and is currently DEAD CODE: issue_actions.request_confirm_build() bumps requested_build_generation as a standalone operator-facing entry point, and the C2 reconcile loop already picks up anything where requested > confirmed. What is missing is the HTTP endpoint and the UI control.

Note the C2 feed only surfaces issues in state='resolving', so a manual build on an issue in another state needs either a state precondition (gate the action to resolving) or a broadened predicate. Gating is the smaller, safer choice and matches the current model: a confirm build confirms an accepted fix, and 'accepted fix' IS resolving.

Cancel is the counterpart to the yt7 bound: an operator who knows a build will never succeed should be able to stop it without waiting for the retry budget to burn.
acceptance_criteria: 1) POST /api/issues/{key}/build requests a confirm build via request_confirm_build (gated: 409 when the issue is not in a state where a confirm build is meaningful; 404 unknown issue). 2) Requesting while a build is already in flight is a no-op or explicitly supersedes it — never double-enqueues (respects the single-flight claim). 3) POST /api/issues/{key}/build/cancel clears the pending request (and the in-flight marker) so the loop stops re-deriving it, leaving the issue in a coherent state. 4) Both actions are exposed on the issue page and gated through issue_state so the UI only shows what is legal. 5) Both emit an event so the audit log shows who asked for the build. 6) Tests cover: request bumps and the loop enqueues; request while in flight does not duplicate; cancel stops re-derivation; gate rejects an ineligible state.
close_reason: Implemented: POST /api/issues/{key}/build and /build/cancel, gated to resolving, event-emitting, wired to Build now / Cancel build buttons. Verified live. Surfacing build STATE remains chf.

title: Runner startup sweeps assume a single runner (no identity/leases)
description: Surfaced while fixing DeltaPorts-i8n. Every startup sweep is GLOBAL and unqualified: reap_orphans transitions all _INFLIGHT_STATES jobs to DEAD, and _reset_building_markers clears all building_generation markers + discards all queued confirm jobs. If a second runner starts while one is live, it kills the first runner's in-flight work. This is pre-existing and system-wide (reap_orphans predates the confirm loop), not specific to build-confirmed resolution — claim_next_job_batch is explicitly written to tolerate a competing runner, so the system half-assumes multi-runner while the startup path assumes single-runner. Fixing it properly needs runner identity + leases (claim rows tagged with a runner id + heartbeat, sweeps scoped to jobs whose owner is demonstrably dead).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A runner's startup sweep only reaps work owned by a runner that is demonstrably not alive. 2) Jobs/markers carry an owning runner identity. 3) Starting a second runner does not disturb a live runner's in-flight jobs or confirm-build markers. 4) Decide explicitly whether multi-runner is supported; if not, make starting a second runner refuse loudly instead of silently corrupting the first.
notes:
CODE PATHS RE-REVIEWED 2026-08-23. The description overstates the damage; the
mechanism is different from what it says and the severity is lower, with one
behavioural edge.

"If a second runner starts while one is live, it kills the first runner's
in-flight work" — IT DOES NOT. _apply_transition (runner.py:458-463) states the
model: "The filesystem queue is the source of truth for what processes next;
the typed jobs table is the UI's read model." Both halves verified:
  - nothing in the processing path reads jobs.state — no `SELECT state FROM
    jobs`, no `== JobState.DEAD` guard anywhere in runner.py;
  - DEAD has NO outgoing transitions, so when the live runner later applies its
    real terminal event it raises IllegalTransition, which _apply_transition
    catches, warns about, and swallows. Work continues to completion.

ACTUAL DAMAGE FROM A SECOND RUNNER'S STARTUP:
  1. Read-model corruption: a live job shows `dead` in the tracker and keeps
     showing it after it completes, because the terminal transition is refused.
     Only the tracker read queries consume DEAD (agentic_queries/jobs.py:34,38,
     overview.py:45) — no behavioural consumer there.
  2. BEHAVIOURAL: _has_active_same_origin_job (runner.py:1418) treats DEAD as
     not-active, so the duplicate-enqueue guard opens and a second triage can
     be enqueued for a port another runner is currently working.
  3. _reset_building_markers deletes queued confirm .job files and clears
     markers. Real deletion, but the intent is level-triggered so the feed
     re-derives; recoverable by design.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM OF MINE: I said concurrent dsynth in one env was
an unguarded physical-corruption risk. Wrong. dsynth_active (runner.py:2106)
pgreps HOST-WIDE and deliberately so — "Process existence is the only state
that actually matters for 'would a second dsynth invocation collide'". A second
runner's dsynth is gated. There is a check-then-act race, but it is not
unguarded.

WHY THIS BLOCKS B3 ANYWAY: every sweep today touches DB rows and queue files —
cosmetic or recoverable. B3's sweep would be the first to `rm -rf` a directory
a live process is building in. Different class of damage, and the reason B3
must not land on unqualified sweeps.

WHAT MAKES CRITERIA 1-3 EXPENSIVE:
  - jobs has no owner column (schema.py:135-151).
  - runner_status is a hard singleton: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 1
    CHECK (id = 1)` (schema.py:180). The 5s heartbeat (runner.py:1611) writes
    that one row, so two runners overwrite each other. "Is the owner alive?" is
    unrepresentable until that table stops being a singleton or a runners table
    exists.
Criterion 4 (decide multi-runner; if not, refuse loudly) is by far the cheapest
and would make B3 safe on its own: one runner means every job-* worktree is
demonstrably ours.

SEPARATE GAP FOUND, NOT IN THIS BEAD: nothing sweeps the inflight/ DIRECTORY at
startup. reap_orphans only touches DB rows, so after a crash the .job files sit
in inflight/ forever while their rows go DEAD. Belongs with B3's crash-safety
theme.

EVIDENCE FOR THE CONTRADICTION THE BEAD NAMES: claim_next_job_batch really is
written for concurrency — atomic rename with the comment "Move lead first; if
that races, try the next pending job" (runner.py:2186-2190).
---

CRITERION 2 DONE 2026-08-23: runner identity is now RECORDED, not enforced.
Multi-runner stays parked; this is only the substrate.

 - jobs.owner_id (schema.py, + a MIGRATIONS ALTER so an existing state.db
   keeps its rows).
 - runners table: runner_id, hostname, pid, started_at, last_heartbeat_at,
   stopped_at. Separate from runner_status, which stays a singleton because
   it is the UI's "what is the runner doing" panel — de-singletoning it would
   have meant touching overview.py:78, agentic_api.py:102, pages.py:632 and
   two tests for no gain here.
 - lifecycle.apply(owner=...) stamps it, COALESCE so an ownerless hook-side
   event does not blank the claiming runner. _apply_transition passes
   runner_id(); the 5s heartbeat refreshes runners.last_heartbeat_at; clean
   shutdown stamps stopped_at, a crash leaves it NULL with a stale heartbeat.

THE TRAP, for whoever does criteria 1 and 3: reap_orphans must stay UNSCOPED
until liveness is queryable. Scoping it to the current runner skips the
previous process's rows — which are exactly the orphans — leaving them
inflight forever and jamming _has_active_same_origin_job, the same jam
reap_stale_queued exists to unstick. Verified by mutation: adding
"AND (owner_id IS NULL OR owner_id = ?)" to the sweep fails
test_reap_orphans_ignores_owner. That test and a comment on reap_orphans are
the guard.

test_job_ownership.py also asserts nothing outside lifecycle.py reads
owner_id, so enforcement cannot arrive by accident without the liveness
machinery.

STILL OPEN: criterion 4. An exclusive startup lock is the cheap answer and
unblocks B3 on its own; criteria 1 and 3 remain the expensive lease work.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23 as an exclusive startup lock. Multi-runner is refused, not supported.

THE FACT THAT COLLAPSED THIS BEAD: state.db is a plain local sqlite file (get_state_db_path, runner.py:364) opened WAL, and WAL needs shared memory, so it cannot live on a network filesystem. Two runners sharing a state.db are therefore two processes on the SAME host, and os.kill(pid, 0) settles liveness exactly. No heartbeat-staleness heuristics needed.

HOW THE FOUR CRITERIA RESOLVED:
  1. Sweep only reaps demonstrably-dead work — satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION, not by scoping. Holding the lock means no other runner exists, so every inflight row is genuinely an orphan. It must be done this way: scoping reap_orphans by owner_id was mutation-tested and BREAKS single-runner restart recovery (test_reap_orphans_ignores_owner).
  2. Identity — done earlier, 7d4b337.
  3. Second runner does not disturb the first — it never reaches the sweeps.
  4. Decide + refuse loudly — done. This was the only real work.

The bead's original premise, 'fixing it properly needs runner identity + leases', is wrong for a parked-multi-runner world. Leases are only needed if concurrent runners are WANTED.

PRIMITIVE CHOICE: fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB), NOT dev-env's CacheLock. CacheLock is mkdir-based and does not release on death — its own error text says to remove it by hand — so a SIGKILLed runner would block every later restart, which is exactly the crash this lock exists to recover from. Verified empirically with two real processes rather than trusting the man page: second acquirer got EWOULDBLOCK while held, and acquired cleanly after the holder was kill -9'd.

The runners table is the diagnostic (describe_lock_holder names pid + started_at + heartbeat age); the flock is the mechanism. The table alone has a check-then-act race between two simultaneous starts.

SEPARATE FINDING, now fixed by the same change: the sweeps run BEFORE main() branches on --once, so running 'agent-queue-runner --once' by hand while the service was up would reap the service's in-flight jobs. --once is gated too, and the test says so.

Exit code 3 (EXIT_RUNNER_LOCKED), distinct from 1 so a supervisor can tell 'already running' from a broken start. Documented in docs/AGENTIC_BUILDS.md.

SCOPE LIMIT, deliberate: the lock is per queue_root. Two runners with different queue roots but the same DPORTSV3_STATE_DB would both start and fight over the read model. Not this lock's job.

STILL OPEN ELSEWHERE: stranded inflight/*.job files after a crash (poly-tr8). Compatible with poly-s9m — a worker pool inside one process is unaffected by a per-process lock.

NOT VERIFIED IN A REAL DEPLOYMENT — poly-4kr still blocks running the services.

title: Block B — Stability & atomization: isolate per build, destroy after
description: Move the build path from 'mutate the shared checkout -> reset it' to 'isolate per build -> destroy it'. Warranted on its own merit (deletes verified-gnarly code), NOT a feature prerequisite. dsynth already isolates its own build slots; the shared git checkout is the real contamination point.
design:
Block B — Stability & atomization: DESIGN OF RECORD
(grounded in a read of the real apply/reset/attempt flow; file:line refs inline)

== D1. Granularity = PER-JOB worktree (settled) ==
The codebase already has a per-job git *branch* abstraction; B evolves it into a
per-job *worktree*. Current flow:
- Patch job runs on branch `bundle/<id>`, REUSED across the bundle's job chain
  (triage->patch); created-from-base once, edits left UNCOMMITTED in the shared
  working tree; branch dropped at patch-job end.
  create: checkout_bundle_branch (worker.py:1505) via runner.py:3231
  drop:   drop_bundle_branch/_drop_branch (worker.py:1604) via runner.py:3394
- Verify runs on a THROWAWAY `bundle/<id>-verify`, force-recut with `-B`
  (worker.py:1709/1754), dropped after the verdict (worker.py:1773, runner.py:3574).
- Attempts within a job SHARE the working tree (attempt_loop.py is only the LLM
  conversation; it does not reset between attempts).

B: replace "checkout branch on the ONE shared tree" with "git worktree add a
per-job working dir on that branch". Create at job start (replaces
checkout_bundle_branch / checkout_verify_branch); DESTROY at job end (replaces
drop_bundle_branch / drop_verify_branch and apply_and_build's _post_build_cleanup).
All attempts in a job share that one worktree, exactly as today.

== D2. THE ONE REAL BLOCKER — gitdir prefix split (load-bearing) ==
Git runs on the SAME physical dir through TWO path prefixes:
- IN-CHROOT `/work/DeltaPorts` (via _exec / ChrootRunner): branch ops, reset_port,
  reapply/materialize, apply_and_build. (worker.py:794; chroot.py:29)
- ON THE HOST `<writable>/work/DeltaPorts` (via `git -C`): ONLY the changes.diff
  capture — _git_diff_against_base (worker.py:654) and emit_diff (worker.py:676).
A linked worktree's `.git` file stores an ABSOLUTE `gitdir:` pointer that resolves
under exactly one prefix. So a naive per-job worktree breaks one side.

FIX (default, no version dependency): move the two host-side diff-capture helpers
to run IN-CHROOT via _exec, unifying all git on the `/work/...` prefix. Then a
worktree created in-chroot is self-consistent. (put_file needs NO gitdir — it is a
plain file write; just retarget its write path into the worktree dir.)
ALT: relative-path worktrees (`git worktree add --relative-paths`, git >= 2.48) —
resolves under both prefixes because the worktree->main relative path is identical
in both views. Requires verifying the dev-env git version; prefer the in-chroot fix
to avoid that dependency.

== D3. Scope: serial (B1-B3) isolates the SOURCE only; the rest stays shared ==
Only the DeltaPorts checkout needs per-job isolation for the stability win. These
are per-ENV (shared), NOT under the checkout, and are FINE shared under the single
serial runner — they'd need per-job partition ONLY for concurrency (that is B4):
  - compose tree /work/artifacts/compose/<target>  (dsynth Directory_portsdir)
  - WRKDIR /work/obj  (make_extract, worker.py:927)
  - genpatch staging /work/genpatch-out
  - module dicts _MATERIALIZE_STATE / _WRKSRC_CACHE / _TARGET_CACHE (worker.py:819,940,948)
So B1-B3 = worktree the source overlay ONLY. Do not touch the compose/obj/dsynth
dirs for the serial feature.

== D4. reset_port's fate ==
reset_port's WHOLE-TREE hammer (`git checkout HEAD -- . && git clean -fd`,
worker.py:1331) exists to stop writes that escaped ports/<origin> from poisoning
the NEXT JOB (worker.py:1325-1330). A per-job DISPOSABLE worktree removes that
rationale entirely — destroy, don't reset. The per-ATTEMPT "start clean" reset
(each attempt from branch HEAD) may be kept, but becomes a SAFE, SCOPED op inside
the disposable worktree (no cross-job blast radius). Net: delete the whole-tree /
cross-job cleanup; keep at most a scoped per-attempt reset inside the worktree.

== Task designs ==
B1 (per-job worktree): new worker.create_job_worktree(env, bundle_id, kind) doing
   in-chroot `git worktree add <wt_path> <branch>` (reuse branch for patch; `-B`
   recut for verify). Retarget the job's paths.deltaports to <wt_path>. Move
   diff-capture in-chroot (D2). Replaces checkout_bundle_branch (runner.py:3231)
   and checkout_verify_branch (runner.py:3462).
B2 (delete cleanup): new worker.destroy_job_worktree -> in-chroot
   `git worktree remove --force <wt_path>` (+ optional branch -D). Replaces
   _drop_branch (worker.py:1604), drop_verify_branch (worker.py:1773), and
   apply_and_build._post_build_cleanup (cli.py:383). Delete reset_port's whole-tree
   reset (steps.py:1083 call becomes a no-op or a scoped in-worktree reset only).
B3 (stale sweep): on runner startup, in-chroot `git worktree prune` + remove
   orphaned worktree dirs whose owning job is not live. Name worktrees `wt/<id>`
   and either pidfile them or diff against active jobs. Replaces "SIGKILL ->
   dirty env -> manual reset-port" recovery.

== Open verifications BEFORE coding ==
- git in the dev-env chroot: version (for the --relative-paths option) + confirm
  `git worktree` is available.
- apply_and_build refactor: today it applies --3way into /work/DeltaPorts then
  _post_build_cleanup; confirm it can instead build inside a per-verify worktree.
- product call: keep the per-attempt "clean start" reset, or let attempts build on
  prior state? (Affects whether B2 keeps a scoped in-worktree reset.)

title: A4 Flaky-aware confirmation
description: A4 Flaky-aware confirmation. A single green is provisional; the next scheduled / 2nd independent green confirms. Guards transient build flakiness (network/toolchain). Prior art: ClusterFuzz 2-bot, >=5/10 reproductions.
design:
## Design

Guard against transient build flakiness (network / toolchain): a SINGLE green is
provisional; require N independent greens before resolving. Prior art: ClusterFuzz
2-bot reproduction, >=5/10 threshold.

**Config:** `confirm_green_threshold` (default 2) in config/agentic-policy.json.

**State:** add `confirm_green_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to `issues`.

**Modifies A2's green handling — first green is NOT terminal:**
- green verdict, `confirm_green_count + 1 < threshold`: stay in `resolving` (the
  "confirming" band — no new state value needed), record the provisional green +
  candidate green-head, and REQUEST ANOTHER build by bumping
  `requested_build_generation` again — so C2 naturally schedules a 2nd INDEPENDENT
  confirm build (reuses the spine; no separate scheduler).
- green verdict, count reaches `threshold`: hand to A2 -> `resolved`; green-head =
  the confirming (last) build.
- 'Independent' = a DISTINCT `build_run_id` / generation, not a re-read of the same
  build result.

**Any red before threshold:** A3 reopen path; reset `confirm_green_count = 0`.

**Depends on A1 + A2** (verdict + resolve path). Optional-ish hardening; the MVP
resolves on a single green until this lands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) confirm_green_threshold config (default 2). 2) issues gains confirm_green_count. 3) First green: issue stays resolving, count=1, requested_build_generation bumped so C2 runs a 2nd INDEPENDENT build (distinct build_run_id/generation). 4) Count reaches threshold -> A2 resolves; green-head = confirming build. 5) Any red before threshold -> A3 reopen + count reset. 6) Test: green,green -> resolved on 2nd; green,red -> reopened + count reset.
close_reason: Implemented + reviewed + committed. Threshold via DP_CONFIRM_GREEN_THRESHOLD env knob (codebase convention) rather than agentic-policy.json.
